scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I've been working at Walmart for about a month now, mainly in the inventory area in the backroom. My job involves handling inventory, and sometimes we have to lift heavy boxes as part of our regular duties. I don't usually interact much with customers since I'm mostly in the backroom. One of my coworkers is a woman in her early to mid-30s. She seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. Let's call her Fcw for short. Fcw approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I agreed, thinking we'd do a team lift. I walked over to the box with her, expecting us to lift it together. But when we got to the box, Fcw didn't go to the other side as I expected. Instead, she just stood there watching me. I asked, "Are you ready?" and she replied, "Yes, it just needs to go in that bin," pointing to a metal shelving unit about four feet high. I said, "Okay, let's do it," and she responded, "It's too heavy for me. Can you please lift it into the bin?" I replied, "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me." Fcw then said, "If you're not willing to help me, I'll find someone who will," and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team, who's not my boss but the most senior person directing us, walked up to me and said, "I just spoke to Fcw, and the next time someone asks for help, you need to help them. That's part of being a team." I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying, "We're both paid to do the exact same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, then she shouldn't have taken the job. I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team, and if you'd like to discuss this further, we can do it with HR present." Feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? It seems like it's two against one, with Fcw and the head guy against me. I need to figure out if I handled this correctly or if I overreacted. First, I need to consider the workplace dynamics. We're both paid to do the same job, which includes lifting heavy boxes. It's part of our regular duties. So, when Fcw asked me to help her lift a heavy box, I agreed, expecting a team effort. But when we got to the box, she didn't lift her end; instead, she just watched me and then asked me to lift it entirely on my own. This seems unfair because lifting heavy boxes is a shared responsibility. If Fcw can't lift her share, then she's not performing her job duties. I'm not the designated heavy lifter; that's not my role. I agreed to help, but I expected a team effort, not doing all the work while she stands by. When the head guy told me that I need to help the next time someone asks, I clarified the situation, explaining that I was willing to help but not to do all the work. I also mentioned that if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I stood my ground and suggested involving HR if needed. On the surface, it seems like I was just stating my case and standing up for myself. But the head guy and Fcw are against me, making it seem like I'm the asshole. Maybe I should have handled it differently. Perhaps I should have been more accommodating, even if it meant doing more work. Teamwork is important, and sometimes you have to go the extra mile for the team. But I also don't want to be taken advantage of or end up doing all the work while others stand by. I need to think about the expectations in the workplace. Is it reasonable to expect that both coworkers share the workload equally? Or is it acceptable for one person to do more lifting if the other can't handle it? Also, considering that Fcw is physically fit, it's reasonable to expect that she can perform the lifting tasks required for the job. If she can't, then maybe she shouldn't have taken the job or should have communicated her limitations earlier. On the other hand, maybe I should have been more understanding and willing to help, even if it meant doing more work. Teamwork often requires compromise and going above and beyond for the good of the team. I'm torn between standing up for myself and being a team player. It's a tough situation because both perspectives have merit. I don't want to be seen as uncooperative, but I also don't want to be the one always doing all the work. Perhaps the best approach is to communicate clearly about expectations and workload distribution. If Fcw is struggling with lifting, maybe we can find a solution together, like using equipment or adjusting the workload. In the end, I think I handled the situation by standing up for myself and clarifying my role, but maybe I could have been more accommodating without compromising my own workload. It's a balance between being a team player and ensuring that the workload is shared fairly.
